roadmapTask: Add an `evalIsolated` action to the chrome-bridge MCP that evaluates a caller-supplied JavaScript expression in the extension's isolated content-script world (exempt from the page's Content-Security-Policy), so that reading page text and structured values works on strict-CSP sites like LinkedIn, github.com and reddit.com where the existing `executeScript` action (MAIN world) is blocked — while keeping `executeScript` byte-for-byte unchanged.

phases.gateRun: Live verification via chrome-bridge MCP on the real github.com sandbox tab (id 1799006098): navigateTo(https://github.com) -> sandbox tab; getTabState anchored {id:1799006098, url:https://github.com/, title:'GitHub · Change is constant...'}; evalIsolated(ISOLATED world; world option omitted, code: document.querySelector('h1')?.innerText) returned Chrome's verbatim CSP-eval error quoting the extension's own MV3 CSP; evalIsolated(location.href) reproduced the same extension-CSP error; executeScript(MAIN world, same code) returned github.com's page-CSP error -- all three on the same tab/expression, so the differentiator was exercised head-to-head but did not hold.
phases.blockedReason: REPLAN_REQUIRED: the horizon's core premise is measured FALSE. A caller-supplied string eval in the isolated content-script world is blocked by the extension's OWN MV3 content_security_policy, not merely the page's CSP. On github.com (sandbox tab 1799006098), evalIsolated (world option omitted -> ISOLATED; `(0, eval)(code)`) returns Chrome's CSP-eval error quoting `script-src 'self' 'wasm-unsafe-eval' 'inline-speculation-rules' http://localhost:* http://127.0.0.1:* chrome-extension://1eaacfc9-e518-4191-a18f-bdf4cfe5d130/` (the extension's own CSP), while executeScript (MAIN, same tab + expression) returns `script-src github.githubassets.com` (github.com's page CSP). The manifest declares NO content_security_policy, so Chrome applies the MV3 default, which forbids 'unsafe-eval' -- and MV3 does not permit 'unsafe-eval' in extension_pages CSP at all. The isolated world is exempt from the PAGE CSP but still runs under the extension's own CSP. Therefore evalIsolated cannot return a strict-CSP value: the same-site-isolated-exemption differentiator does NOT hold (both halves return CSP errors, from different CSPs), and horizon-08 assumption #1 (analysis) is invalidated. The real fix is the CDP Runtime.evaluate pivot (the debugger permission is already declared in the manifest, line 12), which this horizon explicitly deferred. A healerHint fix cannot cover it: the world IS isolated (page-actions.ts:453-508 omits the world option) and the SW IS fresh (the action dispatched and returned a CSP error immediately, not a 30s timeout -- proving the new handler actually ran). Not a stale-build and not a {world:'MAIN'} bug. Next step: REPLAN mode for this roadmap.
phases.notes: Retry (attempt 2) after the chrome-bridge MCP server + dist/extension rebuild (dist rebuilt 15:42/16:15). Attempt 1 was blocked MANUAL_CHROME_CHECK_PENDING (evalIsolated not a callable tool / stale SW). Attempt 2 ran the live check head-to-head on one github.com tab: the differentiator was NOT demonstrated -- both evalIsolated (ISOLATED) and executeScript (MAIN) return Chrome CSP-eval errors, the former from the extension's own MV3 CSP and the latter from github.com's page CSP. The isolated-world string-eval approach is architecturally impossible in an MV3 extension because MV3 extension_pages CSP cannot allow 'unsafe-eval'. This invalidates the core premise that add-eval-isolated-action shipped on: its grade was based on the type-locked surface + unit tests + a correctly-omitted world, with the end-to-end CSP bypass explicitly deferred to this live phase, which now shows no such bypass exists. No amendment was appropriate -- the goal / boundedContext / dependsOn / rubric are not amendable, and the objective (read strict-CSP values) is now known to need the CDP route, i.e. a planning decision, not an execution detail. No override.
